understanding the cellular mechanisms that govern tumor cell invasion.
understanding the mechanisms by which cancer cells migrate through the extracellular matrix.
the physical mechanisms of cell migration and invasion through the extracellular matrix (the ECM).

cancer cells employ context-specific migration programs that are adapted to the local physiochemical properties and geometry of their environment.

the mechanisms of cancer cell invasion through 3D matrices and physiological microtracks differ, and that targeting cytoskeletal dynamics is a potential therapeutic strategy for inhibiting cancer cell migration through microtracks within the stroma.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cancer cells migrate through 3D ECM by a different mechanism than they migrate through 3 D microtracks.

cancer cells employ context-specific migration mechanisms, and that targeting the actin cytoskeleton and microtubules, but not cell-matrix adhesions or traction forces, may inhibit migration through physiological microtrack channels in the tumor microenvironment.
cancer cell migration is context dependent and the mechanisms that cells use to migrate are different depending on the microenvironment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanisms of cancer cell invasion are context-dependent.

the mechanisms of cancer cell invasion are context specific and that we should be thinking about cancer cell invasion in a more context-specific way, rather than thinking about it in the context of a single mechanism of invasion.
cancer cell migration is not a one size fits all phenomenon and that different cell types and different environments will require different therapeutic approaches.
